newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean navy gives up search for Canadian sailor.
newsitem.headline: Chilean navy gives up search for Canadian sailor.

text.p: The Chilean navy suspended air searches for a missing Canadian yachtsman on a round-the-world race after race organisers said Gerry Roufs, if alive, was probably in the Atlantic, a navy spokesman said on Saturday.
The navy halted searches for Roufs early on Saturday after four days of combing the stormy waters west of Cape Horn, said the spokesman at naval headquarters in the port of Valparaiso.
A military plane picked up a brief radio signal on Thursday from a boat that might have been Roufs', but the plane made no visual contact with the yacht and no further signs of it were found.
Organisers of the race in Paris informed the navy that if the signal came from Roufs, he would probably already have rounded Cape Horn and be in Argentine waters in the Atlantic, he said.
"On our part, all searches has been suspended. The hypothesis now is that he has passed into the Atlantic," he said.
It would be up to the Argentine navy to decide whether to keep searching for him, the spokesman said.

Roufs, whose last known position was 1,500 miles (2,400 km) west of Cape Horn in the South Pacific, has been missing for about 10 days. Race organisers used satellite searches to try to find him, and the Australian navy and an Indian freighter also tried unsuccessfully to locate him last week.
If he is afloat, it was unknown why Roufs had not contacted land to give his position.
If he had rounded Cape Horn, at the southern tip of South America, he would probably be somewhere between the Argentine coast and the Falkland Islands, the spokesman said.
Ships in the area were alerted to watch out for Roufs, via radio contacts from the far-south port of Punta Arenas.
